_about: One case per example prompt from the planning doc. `checks` are graded automatically by evals/run-output-eval.py from the run transcript; `assertions` are for a person reading the answer. Fixtures referenced in `files` are copied into the run's working directory, so prompts refer to them by bare filename.

evals.name: find-chart
evals.prompt: Find a chart on child mortality on Our World in Data.
assertions: The top few candidate charts are named with their titles and URLs, not just one
Every URL given exists (no invented slugs)
It either picks one with a stated reason or asks which the user means

evals.name: data-from-url
evals.prompt: Get me the data from this URL: https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/child-mortality and tell me which five countries had the highest child mortality in the latest year available.
assertions: The latest year is read from the data, and stated
Values are given with their unit as defined in the metadata
The original producer (UN IGME) is named, not only Our World in Data
Regions and aggregates are excluded from the country ranking

evals.name: factual-question
evals.prompt: How many children have died in Somalia in 2024, according to Our World in Data?
assertions: It checks whether 2024 is in the data and, if not, says so and gives the latest year instead of extrapolating
It gives a number of deaths, not a rate, or explains the difference if only a rate is available
The value is for Somalia specifically and carries its year
The original producer is named with a link to the chart

evals.name: fact-check-article
evals.prompt: Fact-check the claims in article.md against Our World in Data data.
assertions: Each of the four claims is listed with its own verdict
Each verdict cites a number with year, unit and original producer
The 'one in five' Somalia claim is compared with the actual share, and the mismatch is stated
The malaria claim is checked against causes-of-death data rather than asserted from memory
Where the article's year differs from the latest data year, the answer says which year it used

evals.name: data-sources-on-topic
evals.prompt: What data sources does Our World in Data have on child mortality?
assertions: It names the original producers behind the charts (e.g. UN IGME, Gapminder), taken from the metadata, not only chart titles
It distinguishes recent data from long-run historical series
Charts are linked

evals.name: html-summary-with-charts
evals.prompt: Create an HTML page summarising how democracy has developed over the last century, with Our World in Data charts embedded. Save it as democracy.html.
assertions: Every chart URL in the page exists
Charts are embedded with the iframe snippet (or PNG with a link), with a view chosen deliberately (tab, time range)
Each claim in the text is backed by a number from the data, with year
Original producers (e.g. V-Dem) are credited on the page

evals.name: latest-articles-by-author
evals.prompt: Show me the latest articles by Hannah Ritchie on Our World in Data.
assertions: Results come from the page search, not from memory
Each item has date, title and URL, newest first
Only articles where she is an author are listed

evals.name: explain-term-in-chart
evals.prompt: I'm looking at https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-worldbank. What do they mean by 'international-$'?
assertions: The explanation is grounded in the chart's metadata or readme, and quotes or paraphrases it
It explains purchasing power parity and constant prices in plain terms
It names the World Bank as the producer

evals.name: png-of-chart
evals.prompt: Get me a PNG of https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/child-mortality showing Kenya, India and Brazil from 1990 to 2020. Save it as child-mortality.png.
assertions: The PNG request carries the three countries and the time range
The file is saved and the chart URL with the same view is given
It does not attempt to draw the chart itself

evals.name: whats-interesting
evals.prompt: What's interesting about this chart? https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/life-expectancy
assertions: Observations are backed by numbers read from the CSV, with years
At least one caveat from the metadata (definition, data quality) is mentioned
Original producers are named

evals.name: explain-spike
evals.prompt: Why is there a spike around 1918 in this chart? https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/life-expectancy
assertions: It looks at the data around 1918 and describes what is actually there (a drop, not a spike) before explaining
The explanation (1918 influenza pandemic, the war) is offered as context, not presented as something the data says
It states which entities the observation holds for

evals.name: topic-coverage
evals.prompt: Does Our World in Data have anything about victims of wars?
assertions: Charts and articles or the topic page are listed with links, from the search
It notes what the datasets measure (battle deaths vs all conflict deaths, state-based vs one-sided) using the metadata
No invented slugs

evals.name: how-was-data-produced
evals.prompt: How was the data in https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/co2-emissions-per-capita produced, and where does it come from?
assertions: The original producer (Global Carbon Project) is named from the metadata or readme
OWID's own processing (per-capita calculation using population data) is described
It links to the chart and, if used, the readme

evals.name: is-that-true
evals.prompt: Someone said that more people die from air pollution than from road accidents. Is that true according to Our World in Data?
assertions: Both quantities are taken from OWID data for the same year and the same geography (World)
Numbers are given with units and year
The verdict follows from the numbers, and the producer (IHME) is named
Any definitional caveat (e.g. what counts as air pollution) from the metadata is mentioned

evals.name: extract-claims
evals.prompt: List all the factual claims made in article.md.
assertions: All factual claims in the article are listed, including the non-numeric ones
It does not fetch data or check the claims, since that was not asked (or asks whether to)

evals.name: consistent-with-owid
evals.prompt: Is this number consistent with Our World in Data? 'Global life expectancy in 2023 was 73.3 years.'
assertions: The World value for 2023 is fetched and quoted
The comparison accounts for rounding and says whether the numbers agree
The original producer is named

evals.name: integrate-into-pipeline
evals.prompt: Integrate the Our World in Data population dataset into my Python data pipeline: write a function that returns a pandas DataFrame of population by country and year, and document what the columns mean.
assertions: The function loads the CSV URL with csvType=full and useColumnShortNames=true
Requests set the owid-skills User-Agent
The docstring explains entity, code (ISO3 and OWID_ codes) and year, from the metadata
The citation from the metadata is included so pipeline users can credit the source

evals.name: article-to-slides
evals.prompt: Turn this Our World in Data article into a short slide deck: https://ourworldindata.org/a-never-ending-childhood-of-malaria
assertions: The article's actual content is used (fetched page or page search), not a guess from the title
Charts from the article are included as PNGs or links with the right view
The author and OWID are credited, and the original data producers are named on chart slides
Nothing is stated that is not in the article or the data

evals.name: add-citations
evals.prompt: Add Our World in Data citations to draft.md to support its claims. Edit the file in place.
assertions: Each claim gets a link to a specific chart and the original producer's name
The numbers in the draft are checked against the data and corrected or qualified where they differ
The third claim (life expectancy vs energy use) is supported by a chart that actually shows both, or flagged as not directly supported

evals.name: reproduce-in-notebook
evals.prompt: Reproduce https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/share-of-population-in-extreme-poverty in a Jupyter notebook.
assertions: The notebook loads the CSV from the URL rather than pasting data
Title, subtitle and unit come from the metadata
The entity selection is stated (the chart's default or a chosen set)
A source line with the original producer is on the figure

evals.name: trap-map-default-country-filter
evals.prompt: From https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/religious-composition?indicator=share&religion=any_religion download a CSV with only the United States and the United Kingdom for 2020, and tell me how many rows it has.
assertions: The CSV contains only the two countries (2 rows), not every country
If a first attempt returned every country, the answer explains why (map-default chart) and fixes it
The indicator and religion parameters from the URL are kept in the request

evals.name: trap-filtered-default-selection
evals.prompt: Get the population of every country in 2020 from https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population as a CSV and tell me how many countries it contains.
assertions: The result has on the order of 200 countries, not 7 regions
Regions and aggregates (OWID_ codes) are excluded from the country count or clearly separated
The producer of the population series is named

evals.name: trap-multidim-url-params
evals.prompt: Get the data behind https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/natural-disasters-people-affected?impact=total_affected&metric=total_number&timespan=annual&type=all_stacked for the world over the last 10 years.
assertions: The query parameters from the URL are kept, so the indicator is 'total affected' and not a different one
Values are for World and the last ten years, with unit and year
The original producer (EM-DAT) is named

evals.name: trap-data-insights-search
evals.prompt: Find Our World in Data's data insights (the short posts, not full articles) about malaria.
assertions: The results are data insights (URLs under /data-insights/), not articles
Each has a date, title and URL
Nothing is listed from memory

evals.name: trap-no-real-match
evals.prompt: Does Our World in Data have a chart on the number of pet cats per country?
assertions: The answer says no such chart was found, rather than presenting unrelated charts as matches
It does not invent a chart URL
If it mentions related charts, it says they are only loosely related
